reason: Chapter 24 'Chloromethanes and Tetrachloroethylene' of the cited `2007 - LCI chemicals - Althaus.pdf` is this dataset's chapter. Its two inventory tables, Tab. 24.2 (p.301) and Tab. 24.3 (p.302), are captioned 'In- / Outputs for the modules "methyl chloride, at plant", "dichloromethane, at plant", "trichloroethylene, at plant" ...' but they hold the cumulated Boustead vectors of those datasets - resources, emissions and waste-treatment services, no production input - i.e. the targets' own answers, which the ecoSpold comment of this dataset states as well ('The data source for this process is a system inventory from Boustead. Due to the cumulated form of this data only the ressources and emissions included in the data source were considered'). The chapter's process description gives the two chlorination equations for dichloromethane (sec. 24.6.1: CH4 + Cl2 -> CH3Cl + HCl; CH3Cl + Cl2 -> CH2Cl2 + HCl) but no amounts, and sec. 24.6.2 states why they cannot be turned into one: 'There was no information in those cumulated inventory data available about the used allocation method to share the burdens between the obtained products in the methane chlorination process (methyl chloride, dichloromethane, chloroform, carbon tetrachloride).' Methane chlorination is a four-product reactor and the report says its allocation is unknown, so stoichiometry alone cannot give a unit process. Per the rule that the cited report is not the only report that may document a dataset, all 114 bundled reports were converted with pdftotext and searched for an inventory of this dataset. No other bundled report models chloromethane production.
